newsitem.title: UK: PRESS DIGEST - London Evening Standard - Nov 4.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - London Evening Standard - Nov 4.

text.p: Prepared for Reuters by The Broadcast Monitoring Company

Police and transport chiefs have been alarmed at the huge increase in robberies on board trains and at stations in south London. There has been an increase of 44 percent in the number of reported robberies for the past year, bringing the total 10 984 which is thought to be much lower than reality because many victims have not complained to the police.

Oftel, the telecommunications watchdog is launching an initiative to prevent abuse of market power within the industry in the future. As BT embarks on its takeover of US long-distance carrier MCI to create new company Concert, Don Cruickshank Oftel's Director General is keen that partnerships between powerful groups should not dominate the market to the detriment of customers.

The London Chamber of Commerce and the Centre for Economic Business Research in a report published today forecast that London's economic growth rate for 1996 is likely to be at least 4.6 percent, twice the projected growth rate for the country as a whole. The capital's booming economy is driven by hotel, restaurant and financial sectors.
Cadcentre, the computer aided design company is aiming for a full listing on the London Stock Exchange by Christmas with a value of 30 million stg.
STORE GIANTS AIM TO BEAT BAN ON MALLS

Britain's major league high street retailers are set to take advantage of the last wave of out-of-town shopping complex construction as eight retail parks being built around the country come into being over the next two years. --
